title: Identify the goal
text: We need to find values of $$\frac{2\pi}{3}+2\pi{k}$$ that fall between $$-4\pi$$ and $$0.$$ Since the interval is entirely negative, we only need to test negative integers for $$k.$$

title: Check $$k=-1$$
text: When $$k=-1, $$ $$\theta=\frac{2\pi}{3}-2\pi=\frac{2\pi}{3}-\frac{6\pi}{3}=\frac{-4\pi}{3}.$$ This is between $$-4\pi$$ and $$0, $$ so it is in the interval.

title: Check $$k=-2$$
text: When $$k=-2, $$ $$\theta=\frac{2\pi}{3}-4\pi=\frac{2\pi}{3}-\frac{12\pi}{3}=\frac{-10\pi}{3}.$$ This is also greater than $$-4\pi, $$ so it is in the interval.

title: Check $$k=-3$$
text: When $$k=-3, $$ $$\theta=\frac{2\pi}{3}-6\pi=\frac{-16\pi}{3}.$$ This is less than $$-4\pi, $$ so it falls completely outside our boundary.

title: Compile the list
text: The only angles that fall inside the interval are $$\frac{-10\pi}{3}$$ and $$\frac{-4\pi}{3}.$$
